---
title: Private container registries
---

Many organizations require Kubernetes to pull every image from a private container registry.
This page lists the images that each Posit Helm chart uses.
It also shows the Helm values that point each image at your registry and supply registry credentials.

For a full `values.yaml` file for each product, see the private image examples:

- [Posit Connect](../examples/connect/container-images/private-images.qmd)
- [Posit Workbench](../examples/workbench/container-images/private-images.qmd)
- [Posit Package Manager](../examples/package-manager/container-images/private-images.qmd)

## Images used by the charts

Copy each image that you use into your private registry, and keep the same tags.
The tables show the default image for chart version 0.20.0 and later.
The `posit/` images are on [Docker Hub](https://hub.docker.com/u/posit).
The same images are also on [GitHub Container Registry](https://github.com/orgs/posit-dev/packages) under `ghcr.io/posit-dev/`.
The Chronicle images are on GitHub Container Registry under `ghcr.io/rstudio/`, which the chart sets with the `registry` value.

By default, the charts tag product images as `<appVersion>-<os>`, for example `2026.10.0-ubuntu-24.04`.
Init container images use the tag `<appVersion>`, which corresponds to the Posit product version.
An init container is a container that runs before the main container in a pod.
To pin an exact tag, set the `tag` value next to the `repository` value.

### Posit Connect

| Image | Purpose | Helm value |
|---|---|---|
| `posit/connect` | Connect server | `image.repository` |
| `posit/connect-content-init` | Copies Connect runtime components into content pods | `backends.kubernetes.defaultInitContainer.repository` |
| `posit/connect-content` or your own image | Runs content | `executionEnvironments[].name` |
| `rstudio/chronicle-agent` | Chronicle agent, if `chronicleAgent.enabled` is `true` | `chronicleAgent.image.registry` and `chronicleAgent.image.repository` |

### Posit Workbench

| Image | Purpose | Helm value |
|---|---|---|
| `posit/workbench` | Workbench server | `image.repository` |
| `posit/workbench-session` | Runs sessions | `session.image.repository` |
| `posit/workbench-session-init` | Copies Workbench session components into session pods | `components.sessionInit.image.repository` |
| `posit/workbench-positron-init` | Copies Positron into session pods, if `components.positron.version` is set | `components.positron.image.repository` |
| `rstudio/chronicle-agent` | Chronicle agent, if `chronicleAgent.enabled` is `true` | `chronicleAgent.image.registry` and `chronicleAgent.image.repository` |
| `prom/graphite-exporter` | Metrics exporter, if `prometheus.legacy` is `true` | `prometheusExporter.image.repository` |

### Posit Package Manager

| Image | Purpose | Helm value |
|---|---|---|
| `posit/package-manager` | Package Manager server | `image.repository` |

### Posit Chronicle

| Image | Purpose | Helm value |
|---|---|---|
| `rstudio/chronicle` | Chronicle server | `image.registry` and `image.repository` |

### List the images for your release

The image list depends on your chart version and your values.
To print the exact image references, render the chart with your values file:

```{.bash filename="Terminal"}
helm template rstudio/rstudio-connect --values values.yaml | grep -E 'image(-name|-tag)?[:=]'
```

Replace `rstudio/rstudio-connect` with the chart that you install.
Workbench sets the session images in the `rserver.conf` file, so the pattern also finds the `image=`, `image-name=`, and `image-tag=` lines in that file.

## Authenticate to the registry

Kubernetes needs credentials to pull from a private registry.
You can give Kubernetes these credentials in two ways.

Node-level credentials
: Some managed Kubernetes services let nodes pull from the provider registry.
  Examples are Amazon EKS with Amazon ECR, and Azure Kubernetes Service with Azure Container Registry.
  If your nodes can already pull from your registry, you do not need image pull secrets.
  Go to [Point the charts at your registry](#point-the-charts-at-your-registry).

Image pull secrets
: An image pull secret is a Kubernetes Secret that holds registry credentials.
  You reference it from each pod that pulls an image.
  This approach works on all clusters and does not need permission to change the node configuration.

### Create an image pull secret

Create the Secret in the namespace where you install the chart.
The command creates a Secret of type `kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson`.

```{.bash filename="Terminal"}
kubectl create secret docker-registry private-registry-creds \
  --namespace posit \
  --docker-server=registry.example.com \
  --docker-username=<username> \
  --docker-password=<password-or-token>
```

Content pods and session pods can run in a different namespace than the server.
Connect uses `backends.kubernetes.namespace` and Workbench uses `launcher.namespace`.
If you set one of these values, create the Secret in that namespace too.

For other ways to create the Secret, see [Pull an image from a private registry](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/pull-image-private-registry/) in the Kubernetes documentation.

## Point the charts at your registry

In the examples below, replace `registry.example.com` with your registry host.
Replace `private-registry-creds` with the name of your Secret.
If you use node-level credentials, remove the `imagePullSecrets` entries.

In each chart, `image.imagePullSecrets` applies only to the server pod.
Connect content pods and Workbench session pods need the Secret in a second place.
That Secret covers the main image and the init container images in the pod.

### Posit Connect {#configure-connect}

```{.yaml filename="values.yaml"}
image:
  repository: registry.example.com/posit/connect
  imagePullSecrets:
    - name: private-registry-creds

backends:
  kubernetes:
    enabled: true
    defaultInitContainer:
      repository: registry.example.com/posit/connect-content-init
    # The Secret that content pods use to pull images
    defaultResourceJobBase:
      spec:
        template:
          spec:
            imagePullSecrets:
              - name: private-registry-creds

executionEnvironments:
  - name: registry.example.com/posit/connect-content:R4.5.2-python3.14.3-ubuntu-24.04
    # ...
```

### Posit Workbench {#configure-workbench}

```{.yaml filename="values.yaml"}
image:
  repository: registry.example.com/posit/workbench
  imagePullSecrets:
    - name: private-registry-creds

session:
  image:
    repository: registry.example.com/posit/workbench-session

components:
  sessionInit:
    image:
      repository: registry.example.com/posit/workbench-session-init
  positron:
    image:
      repository: registry.example.com/posit/workbench-positron-init

launcher:
  templateValues:
    pod:
      # The Secret that session pods use to pull images
      imagePullSecrets:
        - name: private-registry-creds
```

The `launcher.templateValues` values apply only when `launcher.useTemplates` is `true`.
This is the default.

### Posit Package Manager {#configure-package-manager}

```{.yaml filename="values.yaml"}
image:
  repository: registry.example.com/posit/package-manager
  imagePullSecrets:
    - name: private-registry-creds
```

### Posit Chronicle {#configure-chronicle}

The Chronicle chart has no `imagePullSecrets` value.
Instead, attach the Secret to a service account and tell the chart to use that service account.
Kubernetes adds the image pull secrets of a service account to each pod that uses it.

1. Create a service account that references the Secret:

   ```{.bash filename="Terminal"}
   kubectl create serviceaccount chronicle --namespace posit
   kubectl patch serviceaccount chronicle --namespace posit \
     --patch '{"imagePullSecrets": [{"name": "private-registry-creds"}]}'
   ```

2. Set the registry and the service account in your values:

   ```{.yaml filename="values.yaml"}
   image:
     registry: registry.example.com
     repository: rstudio/chronicle

   serviceAccount:
     create: false
     name: chronicle
   ```

### Chronicle agent {#configure-chronicle-agent}

The Connect and Workbench charts can run a Chronicle agent in the server pod.
If you enable the agent, set its registry in the Connect or Workbench values:

```{.yaml filename="values.yaml"}
chronicleAgent:
  image:
    registry: registry.example.com
    repository: rstudio/chronicle-agent
```

The agent runs in the server pod, so `image.imagePullSecrets` covers it.

### Use a service account for content and session pods

You can attach the Secret to a service account instead of the pod values above.
For example, you can patch the service account that Connect content pods or Workbench session pods use.
Use the `kubectl patch serviceaccount` command from the [Chronicle section](#configure-chronicle).

## Troubleshooting

If a pod cannot pull an image, Kubernetes reports an `ErrImagePull` or `ImagePullBackOff` status.
To see the image reference and the error from the registry, describe the pod:

```{.bash filename="Terminal"}
kubectl describe pod <pod-name> --namespace posit
```

Then make sure that:

- The image and the tag exist in your registry.
- The Secret exists in the same namespace as the pod.
- The server in the Secret matches the registry host in the image reference.
- The pod references the Secret. Content pods and session pods need the Secret in their own values, as shown above.
